plausibility_notes: Lab isolates donor glass as poisoning route and connects its residue compatibly to stolen original and a used common favor bottle. Strong mechanism support, weak individual identification.
Al's plaster and Brie's cloth fibers support admitted handling but are outside glass; report correctly declines to infer poison delivery from these traces.
Clear shared food and punch reduces bulk kitchen poisoning theory; Brie still has targeted glass access. Clear brush water reduces Vincent's specific container suspicion without exonerating Vincent.
Reed and Justin's portable favor storage rises modestly in relevance because a gift bottle served as an apparent transfer vessel, but all guests had the same favor.
Compatible residue is not exclusive source identification. A lab can support transfer theory but cannot show who transferred, when, or which bottle was emptied and refilled.
Forced lock does not logically exclude a keyholder staging forced entry; phrasing confirm theft is stronger than actual identity implications.
Recovered historical original behind service area and poisoned favor in waste support concealment by someone with sideboard access. Still many candidates.
No actual culprit signal yet: current leaders emerge from glass contact and obstruction, not unique motive. Final evidence must distinguish the broad shared opportunities.
